# F6: Clean-clone reproducibility check

*Generated by `python -m forecast.render_f6_check` from `results/f6_clean_clone_check.json`, which was
written from the checks' own logs and comparison output. Do not edit the numbers by hand.*

## What this check does, in plain words

A portfolio project is only convincing if someone else can rebuild it. This check starts from an empty
folder: it downloads the repository from GitHub with `git clone`, installs the pinned packages into a
fresh virtual environment, adds the Kaggle files, runs every step in order and then compares what it
produced with the committed files, one by one.

### What was run

1. `git clone https://github.com/aradhyachandra/demand-forecasting` into a temporary folder; the
   committed `results/`, `config/`, `docs/` and `README.md` were copied aside as the reference.
2. Fresh venv: `pip install -r requirements.txt`, `pip install -e .`, `pip check`.
3. The three raw CSVs copied into `data/raw/` and their sha256 checked:

{{table:p_raw}}

4. `run_f1`, `run_f2`, `run_f3`, `run_f4` (the full backtest grid).
5. README step 4: a separate `git clone` of the clone, checked out at 1a31ed9 in `.tmp/` (clean tree
   before the run: {{p.r.holdout_rerun.tree_clean_before_run}}), given the raw files and
   `m5_slice.parquet`; `run_f4_holdout` ran there and its forecasts parquet was copied back.
6. `run_f5`, `first_sale_week`, `run_f6`, `render_f6_check`, then `pytest` and `pytest -m realdata`.
7. `python -m forecast.compare_runs`-style comparison of the regenerated files with the reference.

### What was done

1. `git clone` of the local repository at `{{o.r.clone.head}}` into a temporary folder.
2. **Overlay.** F6 was not committed yet, so its {{o.t.overlay_n}} uncommitted source files were copied
   over the clone: {{o.t.overlay_list}}. Generated outputs (`docs/REPORT.md`, `README.md`,
   `docs/figures/f6_summary.png`) were not copied; the clone made its own. {{o.r.clone.overlay_note}}
   Written or edited after the check and so not part of it: this note and its template, the
   processed-files table in `src/forecast/render_f6_check.py`, `results/f6_clean_clone_check.json`, and
   the final F6 entries in `NOTES.md` and `PROGRESS.md`. The template is therefore left out of the
   `docs/` comparison.
3. A fresh venv with Python {{o.r.clone.python}}: `pip install -r requirements.txt` and
   `pip install -e .`. `pip check`: "{{o.r.clone.pip_check}}"
4. The three raw CSVs were copied into `data/raw/` (no re-download) and their sha256 checked:

{{table:o_raw}}

5. Ran `run_f1`, `run_f2`, `run_f3` and `run_f4` (the full backtest grid, part A).
6. **The holdout forecasts.** `data/processed/f4_holdout_forecasts.parquet` is gitignored and has no
   recorded hash, and `run_f4_holdout` refuses a second run because `results/f4_holdout.json` is
   committed. Option (b) was used: the frozen code of commit `{{o.r.holdout_rerun.commit}}` was checked
   out in a separate `git clone` inside the temporary folder (`{{o.r.holdout_rerun.scratch_path}}`),
   given the raw files and the clone's `m5_slice.parquet`, and `run_f4_holdout` ran there, from a clean
   tree (clean before the run: {{o.r.holdout_rerun.tree_clean_before_run}}), exactly as on the original run (module loaded from `{{o.r.holdout_rerun.module_file}}`). Its
   output went to the scratch folder only. The scratch `results/f4_holdout.json` was compared with the
   committed one ({{o.t.holdout_status}}); run-time fields ignored:

{{table:o_holdout_paths}}

   Committed run: started {{o.r.holdout_rerun.comparison.committed.started_utc}}, commit
   `{{o.r.holdout_rerun.comparison.committed.commit}}`, {{o.r.holdout_rerun.comparison.committed.run_minutes}}
   min. Re-run: started {{o.r.holdout_rerun.comparison.rerun.started_utc}}, commit
   `{{o.r.holdout_rerun.comparison.rerun.commit}}`, {{o.r.holdout_rerun.comparison.rerun.run_minutes}} min.
   Every score is the same. The rebuilt parquet was then copied into the clone's `data/processed/`.
   Nothing was changed because of this comparison (recorded: {{o.r.holdout_rerun.nothing_changed_because_of_it}});
   it only checks that the frozen code reproduces. Option (a), copying the parquet
   from the working copy, would have pinned nothing, because the file has no recorded hash.
   Its sha256 in the clone is `{{o.r.holdout_rerun.parquet_sha256_clone}}`; in the working copy
   `{{o.r.holdout_rerun.parquet_sha256_working_copy}}` (identical: {{o.r.holdout_rerun.parquet_identical}}).
7. Ran `run_f5`, `first_sale_week` and `run_f6`, then `pytest` and `pytest -m realdata`.
8. Compared the clone's `results/`, `config/`, `docs/` and `README.md` with the working copy using
   `python -m forecast.compare_runs` (every file byte for byte; JSON files may differ only in the
   run-time fields listed in `src/forecast/compare_runs.py`).
